mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months indicates labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and consumer spending, ultimately depressing corporate earnings and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS (real savings) by more than 0.5% in the same month indicates a loosening of monetary and liquidity conditions, which reduces risk-free rates and boosts risk asset valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS decline by more than 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (payroll employment) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based improvement in demand and labor market strength, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and PAYEMS rise by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, combined with a stable UNRATE below 4%, signals a tight labor market with low slack, which supports wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for 6 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS is above its 12-month MA for six months and UNRATE is below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) above 4% for three consecutive quarters signals a robust demand environment, which increases earnings expectations and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 exceeds 4% annualized for three consecutive quarters.
